query: For an equimolar WTaTiVZr high-entropy alloy made from low-activation refractory elements, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis explains its plastic strain and toughness relative to commercially used pure tungsten under high-temperature mechanical loading relevant to sustained plasma-facing-component service? Specify a controlled comparison that would isolate the hypothesized cause, the observations expected relative to pure tungsten, the applicable boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: In the equimolar WTaTiVZr high-entropy alloy (HEA), severe lattice distortion plus chemical short-range order lower the Peierls barrier for ⟨111⟩/2 screw dislocations in the body-centred-cubic (bcc) matrix; the reduced barrier increases cross-slip probability and dislocation mobility at 800–1200 °C, delaying localization of plastic strain and promoting stable crack-tip blunting. Consequently, the HEA attains >5× higher uniform plastic strain and ≥50 % higher fracture toughness than commercially pure W tested at identical high-temperature loading conditions.
generation.material_initial_state: Cold-rolled and recrystallised polycrystalline sheets, grain size 10–20 µm; (a) pure W (99.9 %) and (b) equimolar WTaTiVZr single-phase bcc solid solution produced by arc-melting + homogenisation + same thermo-mechanical treatment.
generation.intervention: Substitution of pure W by the equimolar WTaTiVZr HEA while keeping processing history, grain size, test geometry and surface condition constant.
generation.conditions: Uniaxial tensile loading and three-point-bend fracture-toughness testing in high-vacuum at 1000 °C, strain rate 1×10⁻³ s⁻¹ (range 10⁻⁴–10⁻² s⁻¹).
generation.structural_mediator: Lowered screw-dislocation Peierls stress arising from nanoscale lattice distortion and chemical short-range order in the random bcc solid solution.
generation.mechanism: 1. Random occupation of bcc lattice sites by W, Ta, Ti, V, Zr generates local bond-length/angle fluctuations (≈1–2 %) that broaden and flatten the lattice potential. 2. The flatter potential reduces the core energy of ⟨111⟩/2 screw dislocations, decreasing the activation enthalpy for kink-pair formation. 3. Easier cross-slip distributes plastic shear on multiple {110}/{112} planes, postponing dislocation channeling and micro-crack initiation. 4. At a crack tip, the lower flow stress enables plastic wake formation and crack-tip blunting, raising KIC.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to pure W under the stated conditions, the HEA will exhibit: • Uniform elongation ≥10 % vs ≤2 % for W. • Tensile yield strength within ±20 % of W (strength retention despite enhanced ductility). • Plane-strain fracture toughness KIC ≥ 50 MPa√m vs ≈30 MPa√m for W (≥50 % increase). • TEM in-situ straining at 900 °C will show screw-dislocation velocities at a given shear stress at least twice those in W, and frequent cross-slip events.
generation.baseline: Commercially pure recrystallised W tested identically: uniform strain ≈2 %, KIC ≈30 MPa√m at 1000 °C, limited dislocation mobility dominated by thermally activated double-kink nucleation with high Peierls barrier.
generation.boundary: Valid for equimolar single-phase W–Ta–Ti–V–Zr HEA with grain size 5–30 µm, test temperatures 800–1200 °C, and strain rates 10⁻⁴–10⁻² s⁻¹. Outside these ranges (cryogenic temperatures, nanocrystalline states, or very high strain rates), other mechanisms (e.g., twinning, grain-boundary sliding) may dominate and the prediction may not apply.
generation.uncertainty: Quantitative values for Peierls stress reduction and exact KIC increment are estimated; direct measurements of dislocation core structures and short-range order in this specific HEA are presently lacking.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare matched W and WTaTiVZr specimens. (i) Conduct high-temperature (1000 °C) tensile tests with digital image correlation to record uniform strain; (ii) measure plane-strain KIC via ASTM E399 at 1000 °C; (iii) perform in-situ TEM straining at 900 °C to quantify screw-dislocation velocities and cross-slip frequency.
measurements: Screw-dislocation velocity vs applied shear stress
Number of cross-slip events per µm of glide
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if, under the specified conditions, (a) the HEA exhibits ≤2 % uniform strain OR KIC ≤30 MPa√m (i.e., no ≥50 % increase over W), AND (b) TEM shows no statistically significant decrease (>20 %) in screw-dislocation activation energy or mobility relative to W.
